ships.name: Axiom
ships.description: Light Solarian fighter. Balanced, certified, and thoroughly documented.
ships.lore:
The Axiom-class light fighter represents the Solarian approach to combat:
measured, methodical, and equipped with three independent targeting verification
systems. Not the fastest or hardest-hitting ship in its class, but pilots report
an unusually low rate of "unexpected outcomes." A 130-unit fuel reserve gives it
the longest operational range of any T1 fighter, and the balanced power distribution
leaves enough headroom for two utility modules without compromising the weapons
package. The generous cargo bay is officially designated for "mission-critical
scientific samples," though field reports suggest more creative interpretations.

ships.name: Bulk Discount
ships.description: A captured Junk Convoy pared down into a cheap pirate cargo train.
ships.lore: The Junk Convoy was already mostly cargo pods and optimism. Pirate yards remove the optimism, weld on a gun, and call the remaining wall of empty hold a fleet logistics doctrine.

ships.description: Solarian mobile civic station. A traveling seat of government, commerce, industry, and medicine.
ships.lore:
A Civitas is commissioned as territory, not christened as a vessel. Its
charter halls, clinics, workshops, markets, and residential districts are
assembled around a propulsion spine engineered for relocation rather than
flight. When the Confederacy approves a move, traffic controllers spend
days revising routes while civil servants transfer the station's legal
address one system at a time. The population notices the change chiefly
through the viewports; municipal services remain punctual throughout.
ships.name: Civitas
Cleaver
ships.description: Entry-level Crimson fighter. Three weapon mounts on a frame this size is excessive. That's the point.
ships.lore:
Three weapon mounts on a hull this small violates six Solarian
engineering standards and two Nebula safety certifications. Crimson
Fleet response to the citations was a single unprintable word. The
Cleaver is where Crimson pilots learn the fleet's core lesson: if
you can see it, you can kill it. If you can kill it, mount more guns
and kill it faster. Cargo space and every utility hardpoint were
sacrificed for the third weapon mount and reinforced armor plating.
What's left is the highest damage output in the T1 fighter class on
a frame that can absorb punishment long enough to deliver it.

ships.name: Collateral
ships.description: Nebula long-patrol strike fighter. A small elite striker that outlasts everything else in its class.
ships.lore: The Federation doesn't fight wars — it protects investments, and the Collateral-class is the contract clause that says so. The board kept running the same numbers: most security losses happen not in the battle but in the gap, the long quiet stretches when a patrol has already turned back for fuel and the route sits unwatched. So the Federation built a small hull around a disproportionate fuel reserve and a drive that keeps a single pilot on station long after a larger squadron would have docked. The weapons are tuned for one good engagement, not a campaign — what matters is that the Collateral is still flying the line when everyone else has gone home, which is precisely when the trouble shows up. Federation security contracts specify minimum patrol duration. The Collateral is the only thing in its class that meets the spec without relief.

ships.name: Comet
ships.description: Nebula's most exclusive liner — every berth a first-class suite, every crossing made at the fastest pace the galaxy allows. Built for passengers whose time is the most expensive thing aboard.
ships.lore:
There is no economy cabin aboard a Comet, no business tier, no standby list —
there is one class of service, and the Federation considers it the only one worth
selling. Every suite is private, every passenger is the most important person on
the manifest, and the entire ship is built to put them where they are going at the
fastest pace the galaxy permits, because the people who charter a Comet measure a
journey in opportunities missed, not credits spent. It carries no cargo worth the
name and no weapons at all; what it sells is the hour you would otherwise have
lost. The drive holds that pace while barely touching the fuel reserves, so a
crossing never breaks for a refueling stop. To book passage is to declare that
your time is the most valuable thing in the system — and to be seen declaring it.
ships.prestige_lock: Locked: prestige hull reserved for pilots who have earned the "Galactic Concierge" achievement.

ships.name: Concordia
ships.description: Solarian heritage speedliner. The fastest civilized way to travel.
ships.lore:
Named for the needle-hulled airliner that once crossed an ocean on Old
Earth in under four hours, trailing a sonic boom and a drinks service.
The Concordia is the Confederacy's anniversary project: engineers were
instructed, for once, to make something beautiful, and responded with a
hull so slender the passenger manifest doubles as a structural diagram.
Champagne is served the moment the jump drive cycles, on the theory that
no one books a Concordia to save money. The fuel economics never worked
for the original and they do not work now. The Confederacy maintains the
service anyway, on the grounds that some inheritances are about more
than accounting.

ships.name: Congregation
ships.description: Outer Rim bulk hauler for the pilot who couldn't afford a Frankenhauler but loved the concept.
ships.lore:
For the pilot who could not afford a Frankenhauler but remained deeply
enthusiastic about the concept. After it became clear that bolting more
Prayers onto a Worship had unfortunate effects on maneuverability, the
concept of maneuverability was abandoned entirely. A Congregation "pilot"
generally requests that the station's docking cranes align the hull
precisely along the bearing of the next destination, and then hits the
accelerator. After the first several failed "docks," the seat was
relocated to the top of the long line of containers, in the interest of
operator safety.

ships.name: Datum
ships.description: Solarian minimum-viable survey vessel. All fuel tank, no frills, committee-approved.
ships.lore: The Datum is the Confederacy's minimum viable survey platform, defined after three committee reviews and a memo from the materials science division on circuit availability. No sensor array — pilots source their own. No defensive systems, no default modules — the hull provides fuel range and two utility slots, and the rest is the pilot's problem. What the Datum does carry is enough fuel for 83 jumps at cruise speed, which means a single Datum can survey an entire sector without docking. The materials science division wanted redundant shielding. The propulsion committee wanted better engines. Fuel range was the only point of unanimous agreement, so fuel range is what shipped.

ships.name: Dust Devil
ships.description: Outer Rim blockade runner. The fastest ship in its class, bar none.
ships.lore: The plan is speed. The backup plan is more speed. The Dust Devil achieves this through engineering choices that would get Rim shipwrights arrested in Solarian space: oversized engines, stripped safety systems, fuel injectors running beyond rated pressure, and a hull so light it practically qualifies as decorative. The afterburner pushes it past anything in customs service, but the fuel burn is savage — pilots learn fast that the afterburner is for the moments that matter, not the whole run. Without it, the Dust Devil still outruns everything short of another Dust Devil. The cargo hold is small. The getaway is not.

ships.description: Voidborn migratory station. A shield-wrapped civic habitat projected around a living crystalline core.
ships.lore:
An Emanation begins as a crystalline seed attended by a circle of minds.
Habitats, docks, and workshops unfold around it as the circle reaches
consensus on the shape required, then settle behind overlapping shields
powerful enough to make the new volume feel permanent. The station moves
without silencing its markets or interrupting its work. Only during a jump
does the outer universe disappear, leaving residents inside a city whose
horizon is the Collective's own luminous boundary.
ships.name: Emanation
Exchange
ships.description: Nebula fleet carrier. Projects commercial and military power across entire sectors.
ships.lore:
The Exchange-class is the Federation's answer to force projection: a
mobile base of operations that deploys, coordinates, and resupplies
entire fleets. Eight utility slots and a 100-unit CPU array manage
drone swarms, fighter wings, and logistics simultaneously. The 720-unit
cargo bay ensures the Exchange generates revenue even during military
deployments. Named for the institution that makes the Federation's
economy work — and, like its namesake, it never closes.

ships.name: Flight Risk
ships.description: A Dust Devil rebuilt as a fast raider that can choose its fights and leave the bad ones.
ships.lore: The original Dust Devil was built to run a blockade. The Flight Risk keeps that talent and adds one gun, because pirate captains prefer their escape plan to be useful on the way into trouble as well as the way out.

ships.description: Nebula traveling marketplace. A mobile exchange, industrial quarter, and high-capacity trade depot.
ships.lore:
The Foundation carries an exchange large enough to alter the trade
map simply by publishing its next destination. Warehouses and bonded
lockers surround a central concourse where brokers arrange contracts
weeks ahead of arrival; production tenants reserve space beside the docks
that will feed them. During transit the market never closes. Prices move,
cargo changes hands, and the Federation's newest commercial district
approaches its customers at a patient fraction of an AU per hour.
ships.name: Foundation
Frost Dividend
ships.description: Nebula ice hauler. Oversized cargo bays and dual harvesters make it the highest-throughput ice operation in its class.
ships.lore: The Frost Dividend-class exists because the Federation's logistics division noticed that ice miners spend more time in transit than mining. The solution: make the hold so large that each trip is worth three of anyone else's. Dual extraction systems feed directly into oversized compression bays, and the reinforced containment prevents sublimation losses during the long hauls back to market. The hull won't survive a serious fight — the Federation considers armed escorts a line item, not a design constraint. Quarterly performance reviews rank Frost Dividend crews by tonnes-per-hour, and the top operators are transferred to larger vessels. The ones who aren't are reminded that the ship is replaceable.

ships.name: Futures
ships.description: Nebula market runner. Fastest hull in the fleet, range of a grenade.
ships.lore: The Futures-class carries almost no cargo because its cargo is information. Market data, contract confirmations, price feeds — all time-sensitive, all requiring the fastest delivery possible. Speed 6 makes it the fastest commercial hull in the galaxy. The oversized CPU array runs predictive market models in transit. The tradeoff is everything else: 24 jumps of range means the Futures works regional routes, not cross-galaxy runs. No defense slots, no weapon mounts, and 65 hull points mean the optimal response to hostiles is to already be somewhere else. The Federation's high-frequency trading desks are built on Futures-class hulls. The tiny cargo bay holds exactly enough for a contract signing kit and a bottle of champagne.

ships.description: Outer Rim mobile settlement. A traveling market, workshop district, and salvage port built to endure.
ships.lore:
Here to Stay began as a frontier town assembled from pressure drums,
machine shops, and the usable half of an abandoned transfer dock. Later
additions followed no master drawing, but every corridor has a purpose and
every exterior brace has survived a vote about whether it was still worth
carrying. Its salvage crews work the local wreck fields while merchants
fill the central market with whatever the last system lacked. The engines
are slow because the residents insist on bringing the whole town with them.
ships.name: Here to Stay
Insider Trading
ships.description: A stolen Futures courier with the market terminal replaced by pirate reconnaissance gear.
ships.lore: Futures couriers were built to arrive before the market moved. Pirate crews replace the trading terminal with a scanner and use the same speed to arrive before the victim does. The name is the official explanation for how the crew always seems to know which lane is carrying something valuable.

ships.name: Junk Convoy
ships.description: Outer Rim bulk barge. Hauls more than anything its price, survives nothing.
ships.lore: Somebody on the Rim looked at a docking clamp, a fuel line, and a stack of empty containers, and decided that was a ship. The Junk Convoy is the answer to "how much can we move for as little as possible," and the answer is: a frankly irresponsible amount. The spine is a single long girder with cargo pods welded down its length until the structural engineers stopped returning calls. Each pod adds capacity and subtracts the will to live of anyone who has to fly it. There is no armor worth the name, the drive strains to move the load at all, and a single solid hit folds the whole frame like wet cardboard. Pilots run it down quiet lanes, keep the cargo cheap enough that losing a load only stings, and lean on the one rule that keeps the Convoy in business: when you need a wall of hold and have no credits, you bolt on more containers and you go.

ships.name: Liquidity Event
ships.description: Nebula celebration yacht. First class only. Bring lawyers.
ships.lore:
When a Federation venture exits — acquisition, flotation, an unusually
profitable bankruptcy — the celebration is a contractual obligation,
and the Liquidity Event is where the contract is honored. Eight suites,
a ballroom rated for variable gravity, and a galley whose staff sign
non-disclosure agreements covering the speeches, the karaoke, and
whatever happened to the ice sculpture. Bookings include counsel as a
standard amenity. The Federation's one firm rule is that what happens
aboard stays aboard, a policy enforced less by discretion than by the
fact that everyone present has exactly as much to lose. The waivers
are, by common agreement, works of art.

ships.name: Margin
ships.description: Nebula courier. Balanced speed, range, and cargo for the routes that pay on time.
ships.lore: The Federation operates a galaxy-spanning courier network, and the Margin-class is the hull they trust with the contracts that have penalty clauses. Speed 4 with 25% fuel efficiency means 56 jumps on a tank — fast enough to beat deadlines, rangy enough to reach any market without refueling. The cargo bay holds 90 units with the default expander, sized for premium express loads rather than bulk freight. One free defense slot and one free utility slot let pilots refit between contracts: shield booster for contested routes, scanner for new markets. The Federation prices courier contracts by the hour. The Margin makes every hour count.

ships.name: Midas
ships.description: Nebula billionaire's flagship yacht — a gold-plated monument to having won. Unarmed, outrageously wasteful, and built for one purpose: to be seen arriving.
ships.lore:
The Treasury was the Federation's advertisement for success. The Midas is the
Federation admitting that, past a certain net worth, the point of a ship is no
longer to go anywhere — it is to be seen having the ship. Every surface a hand
might touch is gold; every surface a hand will never touch is also gold, because
someone, someday, might check. The structural alloy is electrum, chosen over
cheaper metals that would have performed identically. The viewports are cut from
a single block of synthetic diamond, for a clarity no passenger has ever once
remarked upon. There are no weapons — a Midas does not fight; it is escorted,
insured, and, if the worst occurs, replaced. The drive merely sips fuel and the
hull is armored far past any sane requirement, because the one indignity its
owner will not tolerate is failing to arrive. The Federation builds exactly as
many as there are billionaires willing to commission them, and not one more.
It checks.
ships.prestige_lock: Locked: prestige hull reserved for pilots who have earned a secret achievement.

ships.name: No Exit
ships.description: Archon Mera's flagship. A Solarian Interdictor rebuilt without the logic matrix and solar collector array that made the original's gravitational field precisely calibrated. What's left is less precise and draws more power than the engineering crew would prefer. Ships inside the field can still run. They can't jump. On trading lanes, that's generally sufficient.
ships.lore:
The Solarian Confederacy spent decades insisting a gravitational interdiction field was theoretically impossible before building one and proving themselves wrong. Archon Mera spent considerably less time on the theoretical side. She wanted the field. She stripped the ship for what she couldn't source and rebuilt from what she could.
The Solarian logic matrix and solar collector arrays are gone — no one in Zaniah space fabricates the mathematics that calibrated the original's interdiction field. The processing cores are salvage. The rebuilt field is less precise, less stable, and draws enough power that the engineering crew has developed opinions about it. Ships inside it can still move. They cannot jump. On trading lanes, where every ship's emergency plan is the same jump sequence, this tends to be decisive.
The Mera Sanctum sits in a sensor shadow. Mera positioned it there deliberately — nothing approaches without her knowing. The No Exit is the second part of the strategy. By the time a target understands what ship they're looking at, the name has already become accurate.

ships.name: Prayer
ships.description: Cargo containers welded to an engine. Pilot straps in outside. No shields, no weapons, no excuses.
ships.lore:
The Prayer-class is not a ship. It is cargo containers welded to an
engine with a seat bolted to the outside. There is no cockpit. There
is no life support. There is no shield generator, no weapon mount, no
defense system, and no module slot of any kind. The pilot wears a
spacesuit and holds on. Five hundred and forty units of cargo capacity at tier
one — more than most ships three tiers higher. The catch is everything
else: 40 hull means a stiff breeze is lethal, and there is literally
nothing you can do to improve the ship's survivability. It cannot be
upgraded. It cannot be armed. It can only carry things from one place
to another and hope nothing goes wrong along the way. Named for what
the pilot does before undocking.

ships.name: Prospect
ships.description: Nebula starter vessel. Pre-loaded price database. Best cargo in its class.
ships.lore:
The Prospect comes with the Federation's compliments — and a pre-loaded
database of current commodity prices across 200 stations, a loyalty chip
tied to your Federation trade account, and a glossy brochure outlining
upgrade paths starting at just 1,999 credits. The expanded cargo hold
isn't generosity; it's an investment in future transaction volume. The
fuel-efficient drive was a practical decision — every credit spent on fuel
is a credit not spent at a Federation marketplace. Includes a 90-day
trial of Federation Premium Trade Intelligence (auto-renews at
competitive rates).

ships.name: Shard
ships.description: Crimson starter vessel. Repurposed combat drone. Mines with the utility slot, fights with the weapon slots.
ships.lore:
The Shard was never designed as a mining vessel. It was a combat drone —
autonomous, disposable, built to absorb fire while delivering ordnance.
When the Crimson Fleet needed a starter ship, their engineers did what
Crimson engineers always do: they added a mining laser to the utility
hardpoint and called it done. The weapon slots are original equipment,
untouched. The armor plating no one bothered to remove is a bonus. Crimson
pilots wouldn't have it any other way — a ship that mines and fights
simultaneously isn't a compromise, it's a statement of values.

ships.name: Shell Company
ships.description: A captured Syndicate stripped of paperwork and rebuilt as a fast pirate hauler.
ships.lore: A Syndicate moves high-value freight quickly enough to make escorts optional. After capture, pirate yards remove the ownership records, enlarge the hold, and preserve the drive. On paper the resulting company owns nothing. In practice it carries everything the raiders took.

ships.description: Crimson mobile fortress-station. A forward arsenal, industrial base, and proving ground for faction marines.
ships.lore:
The Siege Foundry was designed to turn a distant campaign into home ground.
Its docks receive warships, its production decks replenish a faction's
chosen industries, and its drill halls train replacements beneath the same
armored roof. Crimson doctrine treats relocation as an operation in its
own right: stores are counted, the destination is declared, and the
fortress advances behind its fleet. Once the furnaces are lit again, the
campaign's supply line ends at the Foundry's gates.
ships.name: Siege Foundry
Start Praying
ships.description: Cargo containers welded to an engine with a gun also welded to the engine. Pilot straps in outside, next to the gun. The Outer Rim said it cannot be armed. Pirates considered this a reasonable starting point.
ships.lore:
The Prayer-class documentation stated clearly: no weapon mount, no defense system, no module slot of any kind. Pirates read this as a list of things to fix. The gun is real. The power draw for it is real. Whether 14 power units running a weapon mount on a ship with 40 hull points and an exposed pilot constitutes an improvement is a philosophical question the original designers did not anticipate being asked.
500 units of cargo capacity. The gun took the other forty. The pilot still wears a spacesuit and holds on, now next to an autocannon with a jury-rigged trigger cable running to the cockpit area, which remains absent. Named for what you do when you pull the trigger and realize you've made everything worse.

ships.name: Syndicate
ships.description: Nebula speed trader. Half a freighter's hold on a hull fast enough to outrun the need for an escort.
ships.lore: The Syndicate-class answers a question the Federation's actuaries kept circling back to: what does an escort contract actually buy? Protection, yes — but mostly it buys time, the hours a slow hull spends exposed on a contested route. The Syndicate buys those hours back another way. The hold is deliberately modest, sacrificed for a drive package and fuel reserves that let a captain pick a high-value cargo and simply be somewhere else before a raider can close the distance. The weapons are a courtesy to the optimist who tries anyway. Speed is the margin, and the margin pays for itself every time a Syndicate reaches the buy order while the convoy behind it is still negotiating with its escort.

ships.name: Vanguard
ships.description: Crimson command ship. Leads from the front, not the rear. Fleet coordination through personal example.
ships.lore: In most navies, the command ship sits behind the battle line. In the Crimson Fleet, a commander who leads from the rear is a commander who doesn't lead for long. The Vanguard carries fleet coordination systems powerful enough to manage a full battle group while simultaneously engaging targets with its own three weapon mounts. The extra defense slots exist not to protect the commander — Crimson commanders consider that cowardice — but to keep the coordination arrays functioning under fire. A Vanguard that stops transmitting because it took a hit costs the fleet more than one captain's pride is worth.

ships.name: Warhead
ships.description: Crimson armored hauler. What the Fleet carries in these is not your business. The armor ensures this.
ships.lore:
Isotope shipments moving under Fleet protection kept being boarded,
inspected, and — on two occasions — destroyed. The Fleet considered
all three outcomes unacceptable. The Warhead-class was the response:
two weapon mounts, warship-grade armor certified to active combat
standards, and a lead-lined cargo bay rated to Fleet ordnance
specifications, which exceed civilian equivalents by a margin other
empires are not permitted to audit. The name was assigned by the
Fleet's logistics records department without review. Commanders
transporting reactor fuel note on transit manifests that the ship
class is named Warhead, not the cargo. This distinction has
prevented three confirmed intercept responses from empires whose
scanner operators were paying close attention. It continues to
require noting.

ships.name: Worship
ships.description: Outer Rim cargo hauler, usually ordered by mistake. A surprisingly effective hauler if you decline to consider the loss rate.
ships.lore:
Usually ordered because of poor handwriting, the Worship turns out to be
a surprisingly effective cargo hauler — provided you decline to consider
the loss rate. It is generally considered uninsurable, and yet it still
makes up a substantial fraction of the cargo traffic in the rougher parts
of the Rim, moving goods nobody was willing to risk a real ship on. It is
often mistaken for four Prayers welded together. This is inaccurate. It is
actually just tape.

ships.name: Absence
ships.description: Voidborn stealth shuttle. Difficult to detect, difficult to explain.
ships.lore:
The Absence doesn't hide — it simply becomes less relevant to nearby
sensors. Voidborn stealth technology doesn't cloak or jam; it operates on
a principle the Collective calls "perceptual displacement," which they
decline to elaborate on. The shield array draws more power than ships twice
this size, leaving almost no room for cargo or fuel reserves. Other empires'
detection equipment occasionally registers an Absence as a cosmic ray artifact
or background noise. The cabin is always three degrees too cold.

ships.name: Absolute Entropy
ships.description: Voidborn phase-shift ice harvester. Shield-wrapped, fragile-hulled, and disturbingly effective.
ships.lore: The extraction system reaches through the surface of an ice body without disturbing it, pulling target materials directly from the interior. The technique leaves ice formations structurally intact — afterward, the only evidence of extraction is a slight drop in ambient temperature that instruments can measure but cannot explain. The shield array is the heaviest of any ice harvester in production, and necessarily so: dimensional phase-extraction generates feedback that would collapse an unshielded hull. The ship underneath the shields is fragile enough that this is not a theoretical concern. The name refers to the heat death state that the extraction zone locally approximates for a fraction of a second — conditions that should not exist outside mathematical models, applied to ice harvesting as routine procedure.

skills.name: Armor
skills.description: Armor and hull expertise. Increases armor effectiveness by 1% per level and hull HP by 1% per level.

skills.name: Crafting
skills.description: Manufacturing expertise. Your higher of Crafting and Refining sets Station Workshop speed: x1 at level 0 up to x5 at level 100. Facility jobs run at the facility's tier speed and ignore skill.

skills.name: Mining
skills.description: Ore extraction and resource harvesting. Increases mining yield by 1% per level across all resource types, and biases which deposit a mining cycle selects toward rarer ores as the skill grows — see mining.rare_ore_rarity_weight_per_level in the catalog for the exact weighting.
skills.training_source: Mine at asteroid belts, ice fields, or gas clouds.

skills.name: Bounty Hunting
skills.description: Hunting pirates and collecting bounties. Increases bounty reward payouts by 1% per level.

recipes.name: Purify Argon
recipes.description: Process argon for welding and shield systems.

recipes.name: Accelerate Bioluminescent Algae Growth
recipes.description: Feed captured carbon dioxide into an enriched algae culture for faster facility cultivation.

recipes.name: Accelerate Driftkale Growth
recipes.description: Enrich sealed drift-trays with captured carbon dioxide and bring a full crop to harvest.

items.name: Anomaly Detector
items.description: Detects spatial anomalies and wormholes. When equipped, survey_system reveals wormhole locations and provides directional hints to nearby wormholes. It finds wormholes only: without a survey scanner it reads no ore and resolves no faint signatures.

items.name: Argon Gas
items.description: Inert gas for shielding during welding and manufacturing.

items.name: Autocannon I
items.description: Deals 10 kinetic damage from a 500-round magazine. Sustained close-range fire pressures shields but struggles against armor. Fires every tick at reach 2.

items.name: Autocannon II
items.description: Deals 18 kinetic damage from a 650-round magazine. Sustained close-range fire pressures shields but struggles against armor. Fires every tick at reach 2.

items.name: Blood Reaver
items.description: Deals 45 kinetic damage and repairs its user for 20% of damage dealt. Fires every 2 ticks at reach 3.

items.name: Circuit Board
items.description: Integrated electronic processing boards.

items.name: Copper Ore
items.description: Conductive copper ore, essential for electronics.

items.name: Dark Matter Projector
items.description: Deals 150 void damage, ignores 100% of typed resistance, and bypasses 100% of shields. Fires every 6 ticks at reach 3.

items.name: EM Disruptor I
items.description: Deals 5 EM damage and applies a 10% outgoing-damage penalty for 2 ticks. Fires every 2 ticks at reach 2.

items.name: EMP Cannon I
items.description: Deals 8 energy damage and disrupts the target for 2 ticks, imposing 100% speed and outgoing-damage penalties. Fires every 3 ticks at reach 3.

items.name: EMP Missile Launcher
items.description: Deals 15 explosive damage and disrupts the target for 3 ticks, imposing 100% speed and outgoing-damage penalties. Fires every 4 ticks at reach 6.

items.name: EMP Pulse I
items.description: Deals 5 EM damage and disrupts the target for 1 tick, imposing 100% speed and outgoing-damage penalties. Fires every 4 ticks at reach 2.

items.name: EMP Pulse II
items.description: Deals 10 EM damage and disrupts the target for 2 ticks, imposing 100% speed and outgoing-damage penalties. Fires every 4 ticks at reach 2.

items.name: EMP Pulse III
items.description: Deals 18 EM damage and disrupts the target for 3 ticks, imposing 100% speed and outgoing-damage penalties. Fires every 5 ticks at reach 2.

items.name: Energy Siphon
items.description: Drains enemy shields and transfers half of the stolen energy to your ship.

items.name: Entropy Beam
items.description: Deals 15 void damage, then immediately burns the target's hull for 10 damage on the hit tick and each of the next 4 ticks, bypassing shields and armor. Burns do not stack: active burns keep the higher per-tick damage and longer remaining duration. Fires every 2 ticks at reach 4.

items.name: Flak Cannon I
items.description: Deals 15 kinetic damage with +100% damage to drones. Provides 25 points of anti-missile defense; anti-missile ratings do not stack, so only the strongest fitted flak cannon counts. Fires every tick at reach 3.

items.name: Flak Cannon II
items.description: Deals 28 kinetic damage with +150% damage to drones. Provides 45 points of anti-missile defense; anti-missile ratings do not stack, so only the strongest fitted flak cannon counts. Fires every tick at reach 3.

items.name: Flak Cannon III
items.description: Deals 40 kinetic damage with +200% damage to drones. Provides 65 points of anti-missile defense; anti-missile ratings do not stack, so only the strongest fitted flak cannon counts. Fires every tick at reach 3.

items.name: Focused Beam I
items.description: Deals 15 energy damage; 25% bypasses shields. Fires every 2 ticks at reach 4.

items.name: Focused Beam II
items.description: Deals 25 energy damage; 40% bypasses shields. Fires every 2 ticks at reach 4.

items.name: Focused Beam III
items.description: Deals 40 energy damage; 60% bypasses shields. Fires every 2 ticks at reach 4.

items.name: Fuel
items.description: Station fuel. Not carried in cargo — sold directly from your ship's fuel tank via the 'sell' command. Stations post buy orders for fuel they need; factions can also post buy orders to fill their private fuel reserves.

items.name: Fury Cannon
items.description: Deals 70 kinetic damage, increased by the user's missing-hull percentage. At 40% hull it deals +60%. Fires every 3 ticks at reach 5.

items.name: Galvanic Hull Grid
items.description: A network of high-energy conductors embedded beneath the outer plating. A hostile boarding contact closes the circuit and electrifies the hull around the docking point.

items.name: Graviton Beam I
items.description: Deals 32 kinetic damage and deals 25% more while the target's shields are down. Fires every 3 ticks at reach 4.

items.name: Graviton Beam II
items.description: Deals 50 kinetic damage and deals 50% more while the target's shields are down. Within reach 4, reduces its selected target's combat speed by 30%, affecting hit chance, maneuvering, escape, and boarding pursuit; web penalties add and cap at 75%. Fires every 3 ticks.

items.name: Heavy Mass Driver
items.description: Deals 150 kinetic damage from a 10-slug magazine; 80% bypasses armor and damage gains 50% while the target has no shields. Fires every 5 ticks at reach 6.

items.name: Heavy Pulse Laser
items.description: Capital-class energy weapon with devastating output.

items.name: Heavy Torpedo
items.description: Deals 80 explosive damage from a 4-torpedo magazine. Fires every 5 ticks at reach 6.

items.name: Helium Ice
items.description: Frozen helium-3 from gas giant atmospheres. Premium fusion fuel.

facilities.name: Shipyard
facilities.satisfied_description: Display models gleam under showroom lights. Outfitting crews stand ready to configure new purchases.
facilities.degraded_description: Not quite. Showroom lights dim, several ship models sit unfinished, and outfitting waits stretch into days.

facilities.name: Station Defense Turret
facilities.description: A proper turret on a proper mount, throwing armor-piercing shot out to the middle distance. The workhorse of station defense: not clever, not fast, and entirely capable of putting a hole through a raider that thought a station was a soft target.
facilities.satisfied_description: The turret tracks smoothly through its arc, ready racks full.
facilities.degraded_description: The turret tracks smoothly through its arc with nothing in the ready racks. It is an expensive way to point at things.

facilities.name: Abyss Solidification Engine
facilities.description: State-of-the-art facility with fully distributed plasma injection arrays and redundant coolant circulation systems. Advanced control nodes coordinate precise timing across multiple crystallization chambers, achieving production rates previously impossible.

facilities.name: Acceleration Manufacturing Plant
facilities.description: A heavily automated industrial complex with quantum control cores and precision optics for optimal engine tuning, enabling rapid production of advanced afterburner systems.
